chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Muthannā, from Zurārah, who said:

I was in the presence of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and a man from the people of al-Kūfah said to him, asking him about the saying of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام: “Ask me whatever you wish, for you will not ask me about anything except that I will inform you of it.”

He عليه السلام said: “There is no one who possesses knowledge of anything except that it came forth from the presence of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. So let the people go wherever they wish, for by Allah, the matter is only from here,” and he gestured with his hand toward his house.

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amīr al-Muʾminīn; the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: the matter; here, the authority and true religious source
key_terms.بَيْتِهِ: his house; indicating the household of the Imam عليه السلام as the locus of guidance
key_terms.سَلُونِي: ask me; an expression of comprehensive divinely granted knowledge
key_terms.عِلْمُ: knowledge; here, authoritative true knowledge in religion

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the source of true knowledge in Islam according to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that true knowledge originates from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and continues through the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام. It emphasizes the unique religious authority of the Imams عليهم السلام as the authentic source of divine guidance and truth.
